question: Glueco has 3 different production lines for glue. He needs to determine the number of workers to assign to each production line. On production line 1, each worker produces 20 units of glue 1, 30 units of glue 2, and 40 units of glue 3 during a hour. On production line 2, each worker produces 50 units of glue 1, 35 units of glue 2, and 45 units of glue 3 during a hour. On production line 3, each worker produces 30 units of glue 1, 40 units of glue 2, and 50 units of glue 3 during a hour. Now, Glueco needs to produce at least 120 units of glue 1, at least 150 units of glue 2, and at least 200 units of glue 3. The three production lines can only be opened or closed at the same time. Please determine the minimum production time to meet the weekly demand. There are total 45 workers available. Each line can be utilized by up to 20 workers at a time. Glueco produces 3 types of glue on the 3 production lines.

DATA = {
    "lines": [1, 2, 3],
    "glues": [1, 2, 3],
    # rate[line][glue] = units of glue produced by one worker per hour
    "rate": {
        1: {1: 20, 2: 30, 3: 40},
        2: {1: 50, 2: 35, 3: 45},
        3: {1: 30, 2: 40, 3: 50},
    },
    # weekly demand per glue
    "demand": {1: 120, 2: 150, 3: 200},
    "total_workers": 45,
    "max_workers_per_line": 20,
    "big_m": 1000.0,  # man-hours big-M upper bound
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    L = d["lines"]
    G = d["glues"]
    rate = d["rate"]
    demand = d["demand"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.L = pyo.Set(initialize=L)
    model.G = pyo.Set(initialize=G)

    # Binary: line opened (all lines open/close simultaneously -> at most one)
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.L, domain=pyo.Binary)
    # Integer workers per line (0..20 heads)
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.L, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
                      bounds=(0, d["max_workers_per_line"]))
    # man-hours (line effort) for each opened line
    model.h = pyo.Var(model.L, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
                      bounds=(0, d["big_m"]))
    # common production time (hours)
    model.T = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Objective: minimize production time
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.T, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Demand per glue type: sum_l rate[l,g] * h[l] >= demand[g]
    def demand_rule(m, g):
        return sum(rate[l][g] * m.h[l] for l in m.L) >= demand[g]
    model.demand_con = pyo.Constraint(model.G, rule=demand_rule)

    # Total workers bound: x[l] limited, total <= 45 (only opened lines use workers)
    def total_workers_rule(m):
        return sum(m.x[l] for l in m.L) <= d["total_workers"]
    model.total_workers_con = pyo.Constraint(rule=total_workers_rule)

    # Lines open/close simultaneously -> at most one line is used per period
    def one_line_rule(m):
        return sum(m.y[l] for l in m.L) <= 1
    model.one_line_con = pyo.Constraint(rule=one_line_rule)

    # Link worker-limit logic: if line closed, all its quantities are zero
    def open_link_rule(m, l):
        return m.h[l] <= d["big_m"] * m.y[l]
    model.open_link_con = pyo.Constraint(model.L, rule=open_link_rule)

    def agent_link_rule(m, l):
        return m.x[l] <= d["max_workers_per_line"] * m.y[l]
    model.agent_link_con = pyo.Constraint(model.L, rule=agent_link_rule)

    # Some work must occur on an opened line: if y[l]=1 then x[l] >= 1
    def agent_min_rule(m, l):
        return m.x[l] >= m.y[l]
    model.agent_min_con = pyo.Constraint(model.L, rule=agent_min_rule)

    # Relate man-hours to workers * time on the opened line
    # Each line works for the same common time T, using x[l] workers.
    # Thus h[l] == x[l] * T must hold; to remain linear with bounded T, use Big-M bound:
    #   h[l] <= x[l] * T can't be written linearly, so instead model single common effort:
    # Because only h, T matter for feasibility and objective, we require full capacity coupling.
    def effort_upper_rule(m, l):
        return m.h[l] <= d["max_workers_per_line"] * m.T
    model.effort_upper_con = pyo.Constraint(model.L, rule=effort_upper_rule)

    return model

DATA = {

    # rate[line][glue] = units produced per worker per hour
    "rate": {
        1: {1: 20, 2: 30, 3: 40},

    "demand": {1: 120, 2: 150, 3: 200},
    "total_workers": 45,
    "max_workers_per_line": 20,
    "big_m_time": 1000.0,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    lines = d["lines"]
    glues = d["glues"]
    max_w = d["max_workers_per_line"]
    M = d["big_m_time"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # Sets
    model.LINES = pyo.Set(initialize=lines)
    model.GLUES = pyo.Set(initialize=glues)
    # k = 1..max_w, used to linearise time * workers
    model.WORKER_LEVELS = pyo.RangeSet(1, max_w)

    # Variables
    model.workers = pyo.Var(
        model.LINES, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers, bounds=(0, max_w)
    )
    model.open_line = pyo.Var(within=pyo.Binary)
    model.time = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, M))
    # t_w[i,k] = 1 if workers[i] >= k
    model.t_w = pyo.Var(model.LINES, model.WORKER_LEVELS, within=pyo.Binary)
    # hours_k[i,k] = time if workers[i] >= k else 0
    model.hours_k = pyo.Var(
        model.LINES, model.WORKER_LEVELS, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, M)
    )

    # Objective: minimize production time
    def obj_rule(m):
        return m.time

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Constraint: total workers available
    def total_workers_rule(m):
        return sum(m.workers[i] for i in m.LINES) <= d["total_workers"]

    model.total_workers_con = pyo.Constraint(rule=total_workers_rule)

    # Constraint: workers only if line is open
    def workers_open_rule(m, i):
        return m.workers[i] <= max_w * m.open_line

    model.workers_open_con = pyo.Constraint(model.LINES, rule=workers_open_rule)

    # Constraint: time only if lines are open
    def time_open_rule(m):
        return m.time <= M * m.open_line

    model.time_open_con = pyo.Constraint(rule=time_open_rule)

    # Constraint: link t_w to workers (workers[i] >= k iff t_w[i,k]=1)
    def tw_lower_rule(m, i, k):
        return m.workers[i] >= k * m.t_w[i, k]

    model.tw_lower_con = pyo.Constraint(
        model.LINES, model.WORKER_LEVELS, rule=tw_lower_rule
    )

    def tw_upper_rule(m, i, k):
        return m.workers[i] <= (k - 1) + (max_w - k + 1) * m.t_w[i, k]

    model.tw_upper_con = pyo.Constraint(
        model.LINES, model.WORKER_LEVELS, rule=tw_upper_rule
    )

    # Constraint: hours_k[i,k] <= time and <= M * t_w[i,k]
    def hours_time_rule(m, i, k):
        return m.hours_k[i, k] <= m.time

    model.hours_time_con = pyo.Constraint(
        model.LINES, model.WORKER_LEVELS, rule=hours_time_rule
    )

    def hours_tw_rule(m, i, k):
        return m.hours_k[i, k] <= M * m.t_w[i, k]

    model.hours_tw_con = pyo.Constraint(
        model.LINES, model.WORKER_LEVELS, rule=hours_tw_rule
    )

    # Constraint: hours_k[i,k] >= time - M*(1 - t_w[i,k])  (forces equality when open)
    def hours_force_rule(m, i, k):
        return m.hours_k[i, k] >= m.time - M * (1 - m.t_w[i, k])

    model.hours_force_con = pyo.Constraint(
        model.LINES, model.WORKER_LEVELS, rule=hours_force_rule
    )

    # Constraint: demand satisfaction per glue type
    # total production of glue g = sum_{i,k} rate[i,g] * hours_k[i,k]
    def demand_rule(m, g):
        return (
            sum(
                d["rate"][i][g] * m.hours_k[i, k]
                for i in m.LINES
                for k in m.WORKER_LEVELS
            )
            >= d["demand"][g]
        )

    model.demand_con = pyo.Constraint(model.GLUES, rule=demand_rule)

    return model

    "total_workers": 45,
    # "Each line can be utilized by up to 20 workers at a time"
    "line_capacity": 20,
    # upper bound on production time used for big-M (safe: with 1 worker at min rate 20/h, 200 units -> 10h; use generous 45)
    "T_max": 45,
    "lines": [1, 2, 3],
    "glues": [1, 2, 3],
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    m.L = pyo.Set(initialize=d["lines"])
    m.G = pyo.Set(initialize=d["glues"])
    m.K = pyo.RangeSet(1, d["line_capacity"])  # binary expansion positions per line

    # z = 1 if the lines are open (they open/close simultaneously)
    m.z = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.Binary)
    # T = production time in hours
    m.T = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, d["T_max"]))
    # b[l,k] binary expansion of workers on line l: x[l] = sum_k b[l,k]
    m.b = pyo.Var(m.L, m.K, domain=pyo.Binary)
    # u[l,k] = T * b[l,k]  (McCormick linearisation, exact for binary b)
    m.u = pyo.Var(m.L, m.K, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, d["T_max"]))

    # objective: minimum production time
    m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=m.T, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # demand per glue type: sum_l rate[g,l] * (T * x[l]) >= demand[g]
    def demand_rule(m, g):
        return sum(d["rate"][l][g] * sum(m.u[l, k] for k in m.K) for l in m.L) >= d["demand"][g]
    m.demand = pyo.Constraint(m.G, rule=demand_rule)

    # total workers available
    def total_rule(m):
        return sum(sum(m.b[l, k] for k in m.K) for l in m.L) <= d["total_workers"]
    m.total_workers = pyo.Constraint(rule=total_rule)

    # simultaneous opening: workers on line l only if z = 1
    def open_rule(m, l):
        return sum(m.b[l, k] for k in m.K) <= d["line_capacity"] * m.z
    m.open_link = pyo.Constraint(m.L, rule=open_rule)

    # McCormick linearisation of u[l,k] = T * b[l,k]
    def mc1(m, l, k):
        return m.u[l, k] <= d["T_max"] * m.b[l, k]
    m.mc1 = pyo.Constraint(m.L, m.K, rule=mc1)

    def mc2(m, l, k):
        return m.u[l, k] <= m.T
    m.mc2 = pyo.Constraint(m.L, m.K, rule=mc2)

    def mc3(m, l, k):
        return m.u[l, k] >= m.T - d["T_max"] * (1 - m.b[l, k])
    m.mc3 = pyo.Constraint(m.L, m.K, rule=mc3)

    return m

#   (2) Glue 2 demand:  sum_i rate2[i] * w[i] >= 150

#   (9) w[i] = sum_k k * u[i,k]
#   (10) u[i,k] <= M * z[i,k]
#   (11) u[i,k] <= t
#   (12) u[i,k] >= t - M * (1 - z[i,k])
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    model.G = pyo.Set(initialize=glues)

                      bounds=(0, max_per_line))
    model.t = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, M))
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.L, domain=pyo.Binary)
    model.z = pyo.Var(model.L, model.K, domain=pyo.Binary)
    model.u = pyo.Var(model.L, model.K, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals,

    model.w = pyo.Var(model.L, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals,

    # Objective: minimize production time
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.t, sense=pyo.minimize)

    m.G = pyo.Set(initialize=d["glues"])
    m.K = pyo.Set(initialize=list(range(d["max_workers_per_line"] + 1)))

    # binselect[l,k] = 1 if line l runs with exactly k workers
    m.binselect = pyo.Var(m.L, m.K, domain=pyo.Binary)
    # operating time t hours (same for all lines, since lines open/close together)
    m.t = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, d["time_upper"]))
    # plant status
    m.on = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.Binary)
    # hsel[l,k] linearises t * binselect[l,k]
    m.hsel = pyo.Var(m.L, m.K, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
                     bounds=(0, d["time_upper"]))

    M = d["time_upper"]

    def c_one_per_line(m, l):
        return sum(m.binselect[l, k] for k in m.K) == 1
    m.c_one_per_line = pyo.Constraint(m.L, rule=c_one_per_line)

    # hsel lies between t and binselect*t (McCormick with binary)
    def c_hsel_le_m(m, l, k):
        return m.hsel[l, k] <= M * m.binselect[l, k]
    m.c_hsel_le_m = pyo.Constraint(m.L, m.K, rule=c_hsel_le_m)

    def c_hsel_le_t(m, l, k):
        return m.hsel[l, k] <= m.t
    m.c_hsel_le_t = pyo.Constraint(m.L, m.K, rule=c_hsel_le_t)

    def c_hsel_ge_t(m, l, k):
        return m.hsel[l, k] >= m.t - M * (1 - m.binselect[l, k])
    m.c_hsel_ge_t = pyo.Constraint(m.L, m.K, rule=c_hsel_ge_t)

    # Only open plant means any positive-time choice can be active
    def c_on_binary(m, l):
        return sum(k * m.binselect[l, k] for k in m.K) <= d["max_workers_per_line"] * m.on
    m.c_on_binary = pyo.Constraint(m.L, rule=c_on_binary)

    def c_time_open(m):
        return m.t <= M * m.on
    m.c_time_open = pyo.Constraint(rule=c_time_open)

    # total workers across lines
    def c_total_workers(m):
        return sum((k * m.binselect[l, k]) for l in m.L for k in m.K) <= d["total_workers"]
    m.c_total_workers = pyo.Constraint(rule=c_total_workers)

    # total worker-hours on line l = sum_k k * hsel[l,k]
    def c_demand(m, g):
        return sum(d["rate"][(l, g)] * sum(k * m.hsel[l, k] for k in m.K)
                   for l in m.L) >= d["demand"][g]
    m.c_demand = pyo.Constraint(m.G, rule=c_demand)

    # each line individually more than zero directly using hsel bound l,k logic/identical
    # worker-count cap by slots not strictly needed because of model cap on use and hsel per 'line'. Capacity<=20 enforced via
    #  binselection sum and constraints above; explicit line-level max workers:
    def c_cap(m, l):
        return sum(k * m.binselect[l, k] for k in m.K) <= d["max_workers_per_line"]
    m.c_cap = pyo.Constraint(m.L, rule=c_cap)

    def obj_rule(m):
        return m.t
    m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    return m

def build_model(data=None):

    # Sets

    model.G = pyo.Set(initialize=d["glues"])

    model.t = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    # n[i] = worker-hours spent on line i
    model.n = pyo.Var(model.L, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    # w = 1 if production lines are open (all together), else 0
    model.w = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.Binary)

    # Objective: minimise production time
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.t, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Demand constraints: total units of each glue >= demand
    # sum_i rate[i,j]*n[i] >= demand[j]
    def demand_rule(m, j):
        return sum(d["rate"][(i, j)] * m.n[i] for i in m.L) >= d["demand"][j]
    model.demand_con = pyo.Constraint(model.G, rule=demand_rule)

    def linecap_rule(m, i):
        return m.n[i] <= d["line_worker_cap"] * m.t
    model.linecap_con = pyo.Constraint(model.L, rule=linecap_rule)

    # Total simultaneous workers: sum_i n[i] <= 45 * t
    def totalcap_rule(m):
        return sum(m.n[i] for i in m.L) <= d["total_workers"] * m.t
    model.totalcap_con = pyo.Constraint(rule=totalcap_rule)

    # Open/close linkage: all lines together, if closed no worker-hours
    def open_rule(m, i):
        return m.n[i] <= d["big_m"] * m.w
    model.open_con = pyo.Constraint(model.L, rule=open_rule)

    def time_link_rule(m):
        return m.t <= d["big_m"] * m.w
    model.time_link_con = pyo.Constraint(rule=time_link_rule)

"""
Glueco production-line staffing / minimum production time model.

DECISION VARIABLES
------------------
x[i]  : number of workers assigned to production line i (i in {1,2,3})
        domain: NonNegativeIntegers, bounds (0, max_workers_per_line)
y[i]  : binary, 1 if line i is open (used), 0 otherwise
        domain: Binary
T     : production time in hours (common to all lines, since all lines
        open/close together and run simultaneously)
        domain: NonNegativeReals

OBJECTIVE (in words)
--------------------
Minimise the total production time T needed to meet all glue demands.

CONSTRAINTS (numbered, with source sentence)
--------------------------------------------
(1) For each glue type g: total output over all lines must be at least the
    demand for g.  Output of line i for glue g = rate[i][g] * x[i] * T.
    This is bilinear (x[i]*T), so we linearise using the standard
    "workers-hours" trick: define w[i] = x[i] * T (worker-hours on line i).
    Then output = rate[i][g] * w[i], which is linear in w.
    Source: "needs to produce at least 120 units of glue 1, at least 150
    units of glue 2, and at least 200 units of glue 3."
(2) Total workers used across all lines <= total_workers (45).
    Source: "There are total 45 workers available."
(3) Each line can use at most max_workers_per_line (20) workers.
    Source: "Each line can be utilized by up to 20 workers at a time."
(4) Linking w[i] = x[i] * T via big-M (McCormick / binary on/off):
    w[i] <= max_workers_per_line * T
    w[i] <= max_workers_per_line * y[i] * T_max   -> handled with T bound
    w[i] >= 0
    Since T is bounded above by T_max, we use:
        w[i] <= max_workers_per_line * T
        w[i] <= T_max * x[i]
        w[i] >= 0
    and x[i] <= max_workers_per_line * y[i] (line open if workers assigned).
(5) All lines open/close together: y[i] equal for all i.  We enforce this
    by using a single binary variable y for all lines.
    Source: "The three production lines can only be opened or closed at the
    same time."

Note: T_max is a safe upper bound on production time.  A valid bound is
obtained by noting that with 1 worker on the slowest line, demand 200 of
glue 3 at rate 40/hr needs 5 hours; we use a generous bound of 1000.
"""

import pyomo.environ as pyo

GOLD_ANSWER = None

DATA = {
    # rate[line][glue_type] = units produced per worker per hour
    "rate": {
        1: {1: 20, 2: 30, 3: 40},
        2: {1: 50, 2: 35, 3: 45},
        3: {1: 30, 2: 40, 3: 50},
    },
    "demand": {1: 120, 2: 150, 3: 200},
    "total_workers": 45,
    "max_workers_per_line": 20,
    "T_max": 1000,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    lines = sorted(d["rate"].keys())
    glues = sorted(d["demand"].keys())

    m = pyo.ConcreteModel(name="Glueco")

    m.L = pyo.Set(initialize=lines)
    m.G = pyo.Set(initialize=glues)

    # Decision variables
    m.x = pyo.Var(
        m.L,
        within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
        bounds=(0, d["max_workers_per_line"]),
    )
    m.w = pyo.Var(m.L, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, None))
    m.y = pyo.Var(within=pyo.Binary)
    m.T = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, d["T_max"]))

    # (1) Demand constraints: sum_i rate[i][g] * w[i] >= demand[g]
    def demand_rule(mdl, g):
        return sum(d["rate"][i][g] * mdl.w[i] for i in mdl.L) >= d["demand"][g]

    m.demand_con = pyo.Constraint(m.G, rule=demand_rule)

    # (2) Total workers available
    def total_workers_rule(mdl):
        return sum(mdl.x[i] for i in mdl.L) <= d["total_workers"]

    m.total_workers_con = pyo.Constraint(rule=total_workers_rule)

    # (3) Per-line worker cap already in bounds; add explicit constraint for clarity
    def line_cap_rule(mdl, i):
        return mdl.x[i] <= d["max_workers_per_line"]

    m.line_cap_con = pyo.Constraint(m.L, rule=line_cap_rule)

    # (4) Linearisation of w[i] = x[i] * T
    # w[i] <= max_workers_per_line * T
    def w_le_T_rule(mdl, i):
        return mdl.w[i] <= d["max_workers_per_line"] * mdl.T

    m.w_le_T_con = pyo.Constraint(m.L, rule=w_le_T_rule)

    # w[i] <= T_max * x[i]
    def w_le_x_rule(mdl, i):
        return mdl.w[i] <= d["T_max"] * mdl.x[i]

    m.w_le_x_con = pyo.Constraint(m.L, rule=w_le_x_rule)

    # (5) All lines open/close together: x[i] <= max_workers_per_line * y
    def open_link_rule(mdl, i):
        return mdl.x[i] <= d["max_workers_per_line"] * mdl.y

    m.open_link_con = pyo.Constraint(m.L, rule=open_link_rule)

    # Objective: minimise production time T
    m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=m.T, sense=pyo.minimize)

    return m
